mechanics.name: Self-Preservation
mechanics.currentEffect: Whenever another Survivor is hooked, you gain Elusive for 13/14/15 seconds. Elusive suppresses your Aura, Scratch Marks, Pools of Blood, and Grunts of Pain.
activation: Ends/deactivates when: Elusive expires after 13/14/15 seconds; Elusive may also end early under its status-effect rules.
mechanics.patchNote: Latest live balance change (10.2.0): Reduced Elusive duration after another Survivor is hooked from 20/25/30 to 13/14/15 seconds.
mechanics.plainEnglishSummary: When another Survivor is hooked, briefly hides your Aura and tracking traces from the Killer.
specialInteractions: Elusive hides the Survivor's Aura and suppresses Scratch Marks, Pools of Blood, and Grunts of Pain.

editorial.summary: Whenever another Survivor is hooked, gain Elusive for up to 15 seconds, suppressing Aura, Scratch Marks, Blood, and pain sounds.
useCases: Rotate safely after another Survivor is hooked while common post-hook information perks may be active.
Hide several tracking channels at once during a dangerous Killer rotation.
Continue a nearby objective with reduced risk of being immediately located.
counters: The perk only triggers when another Survivor is hooked.
Killer Instinct, direct sight, and other non-covered information can still reveal you.
If the Killer does not rotate toward you, much of the 13/14/15-second protection may be unnecessary.
Basekit post-unhook Elusive overlaps part of this perk's tracking-denial value during the first 10 seconds after rescue.
pros: Elusive suppresses multiple tracking channels simultaneously.
Automatic trigger with no execution requirement.
Current 9.5-era design is much broader than the perk's older form.
cons: Does not help when you are the Survivor being hooked.
Protection may be wasted if the Killer remains near the hook or chases someone else.
analysis: Self-Preservation kept the same broad Elusive package in 10.2 but lost half of its old Tier III duration, falling from thirty seconds to fifteen.

Fifteen seconds is still enough to hide a post-hook rotation or remain on a nearby objective through common Aura-reading windows. The effect continues to suppress several tracking channels at once rather than one specific cue.
The shorter window makes wasted triggers more painful. If the Killer stays on the hooked Survivor or rotates elsewhere, the protection can expire before it is tested.
The perk remains useful, especially in Solo Q, but its old ranking should come down because the duration nerf directly attacks its consistency.
editorial.verdict: Same strong Elusive package, much shorter clock. Self-Preservation is still useful after teammate hooks, but 15 seconds demands better timing than the old 30.
